title: Localized tensor comparison inverse-shift conjugacy square
statement: Let R,A,B,C be commutative rings in one universe, A and B R-algebras, C an algebra over E=A tensor_R B, and fix derived categories of R-, A- and B-modules. Let F be termwise extension from A to C. Fix A-complexes U,Q, a C-complex N and a map t:F(Q) to N. Given a base-derived tensor cohomology model mU of U tensor Q, integers n and i, there exist a model mV of U[-n] tensor Q, a C-linear source isomorphism eS: C tensor_E mV.cohomology(i+n) to C tensor_E mU.cohomology(i), and a target isomorphism eT: H^(i+n)(F(U[-n]) tensor_C N) to H^i(F(U) tensor_C N), such that the degree-i localized comparison followed by H^i(mu_F(U,Q)^(-1) then F(U) tensor t) equals eS^(-1), followed by the corresponding degree-(i+n) comparison for U[-n], followed by eT. No K-flatness or invertibility hypothesis is imposed. Models and comparisons are those of [def-pc-base-derived-tensor-cohomology-model]; the coefficient map and tensor conventions are those of [def-pc-localized-tensor-comparison-property].

mathlib_searches.query: Natural cohomology shift square for the counit of a left derived extension of scalars functor
mathlib_searches.results: Eight hits including derived adjunction counit and exact-functor shift instances; none supplies the base-derived tensor cohomology model conjugacy.
The first-variable total tensor shift isomorphism and naturality lemmas exist in Mathlib.Algebra.Homology.BifunctorShift; they do not transport our cohomology model.

mathlib_searches.query: Cohomology comparison for a left derived functor commutes with integer shifts
shift.*square|shift.*cohomology.*model and shift.*counit|counit.*shift|commShift in homology and derived-functor modules
mathlib_searches.results: No specialized model transport in Sheaf or WeilConjectures. Mathlib tensor shift and cohomology shift maps are available; no single specialized conjugacy theorem.

proof.text: Use CochainComplex.mapBifunctorShift₁Iso on U,Q at -n, and the additive scalar-extension shift isomorphisms, to identify U[-n] tensor Q with (U tensor Q)[-n] and its scalar extensions. Retain mU.derived, mU.counit and mU.universal. Uniqueness of the total left derived functor supplies its shift comparison compatible with the counit. Reindex mU.cohomology by j -> j-n and use this derived shift comparison to define the cohomologyIso for the new complex. Naturality in multiplication by a in A and B-linearity preserve the E-action and prove cohomologyIso_smul.

Transport ordinaryIso and ordinaryToLocalized through the scalar-extension shift isomorphisms and the tensor shift isomorphism. Their generator formulas are unchanged. Define comparison using comparison_eq, with the transported cohomologyIso and counit. Naturality under multiplication by A shows it is E-linear. Define localizedComparison by extension/restriction adjunction; its unit identity is localized_eq. These constructions give the model mV; no arbitrary model existence witness is selected.

At j=i+n the cohomology shift comparison identifies the reindexed E-cohomology with mU.cohomology i; apply extension to C to obtain eS. Apply the cohomology shift map to the first-variable tensor shift and the scalar-extension shift map to obtain eT. Naturality of tensor shift in t and compatibility with the monoidal comparison of F give the target square. Counit shift compatibility, comparison_eq and transposition through localized_eq give the source square. Compose the two squares and cancel inverse shift isomorphisms to get the stated conjugacy. The first-variable tensor shift has no extra signs. For n=0 these are the zero-shift comparisons; for zero complexes or t=0 the same naturality equations apply.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_localizedTensorComparison_shift_square
    (U : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ) (n : ℤ)
    (mU : BaseDerivedTensorCohomologyModel R A B (U ⊗ Q) C) (i : ℤ) :
    let F := (extendScalars.{u, u, u}
      ((algebraMap (A ⊗[R] B) C).comp (algebraMap A (A ⊗[R] B)))).mapHomologicalComplex
        (.up ℤ)
    ∃ (mV : BaseDerivedTensorCohomologyModel R A B ((U⟦-n⟧) ⊗ Q) C)
      (eS : (extendScalars (algebraMap (A ⊗[R] B) C)).obj (mV.cohomology (i + n)) ≅
        (extendScalars (algebraMap (A ⊗[R] B) C)).obj (mU.cohomology i))
      (eT : (F.obj (U⟦-n⟧) ⊗ N).homology (i + n) ≅ (F.obj U ⊗ N).homology i),
    mU.localizedComparison i ≫ HomologicalComplex.homologyMap
      ((Functor.Monoidal.μIso F U Q).inv ≫ (F.obj U ◁ t)) i =
    eS.inv ≫ (mV.localizedComparison (i + n) ≫ HomologicalComplex.homologyMap
      ((Functor.Monoidal.μIso F (U⟦-n⟧) Q).inv ≫ (F.obj (U⟦-n⟧) ◁ t)) (i + n)) ≫
        eT.hom
